hed: A Quiet Morning on the Desk
deck: Table Rock this morning: 911.74 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Streamer on the generate.
play.body: When SWPA spins it, Taneycomo becomes a small river. A dark wooly bugger in the seams.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 912.55 early in the week to 911.74 this morning — about 0.81 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. Live USACE reading 12:00 CT: 911.74 ft, 20 cfs through the dam. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: The lake is sitting approximately 3 ft below full pool, exposing more shoreline, stumps, and hazards in shallow coves, upper arms, and near some ramps. Boaters should use extra caution, especially in the James, Kings, and Long Creek arms where navigation can be tighter.

Surface water has been in the low- to mid-70s with excellent clarity in recent readings. Bass have responded well to topwaters and soft plastics early, then jigs, live bait, or drop-shot rigs around long points, gravel flats dropping into 20–40 ft, and offshore structure. Mixed-bag action continues with walleye on points in 20–25 ft and crappie or spotted bass coming from deeper brush and docks. Recent trips have produced solid numbers, including 20+ bass some mornings. The low water also means longer walks at certain launches.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~20 cfs at 12:00 CT (USACE live). Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: This cold tailwater stays productive year-round thanks to deep releases from Table Rock and steady stocking. Generation remains the primary tactic book: low or minimal flows overnight and early create prime windows for wading, light-line drifting, or indicator fishing, while stronger current (typically building afternoon into evening) calls for weighted rigs and precise drifts through seams and behind structure.

From Table Rock Dam down to Fall Creek is trophy water — artificial lures and flies only; no soft plastics or scented/natural baits. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released. Save pink worms, PowerBait, or other soft plastics/scented baits for the water below Fall Creek and state that clearly. A trout permit is required to keep fish. Recent September patterns show strong action on micro jigs (brown, black, white, sculpin), mega worms, midges, scuds, and hoppers during low windows, with black jigs shining after dark. Water clarity is excellent — clean presentations win. Call 866-494-1993 for the latest SWPA schedule before you wade or launch.

editor.note: Two-lake daily rebuilt from the morning fishing scout plus the prior week of files. We print a level only when the scout had one. Carry-forward mornings are labeled. No invented bite ratings. Call 866-494-1993 before wading Taneycomo.
